questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Residual Entropy and Degenerate Ground States under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
For a frustrated magnet, many configurations can remain equal-energy ground states, so \(\Omega_0\gt 1\) in equation \([1]\) even in equilibrium. For a glass, configurations are trapped because relaxation becomes too slow; equation \([5]\) describes the frozen distribution, but the state is not internal equilibrium. Final result: ground-state degeneracy produces equilibrium multiplicity, whereas a glass retains nonequilibrium configurational disorder; either can give nonzero residual entropy.

Final answer:
